the trait of being spurred on by a dislike of falling below your standards
a group of lions
unreasonable and inordinate self-esteem (personified as one of the deadly sins)

vi_block: Sự kiêu hãnh, sự hãnh diện; niềm kiêu hãnh, niềm hãnh diện, tính tự cao, tính tự phụ, tính kiêu căng.
Lòng tự trọng; lòng tự hào về công việc của mình.
Độ đẹp nhất, độ rực rỡ nhất, độ chín muồi, độ phát triển nhất.
Sự tráng lệ, sự huy hoàng, sự lộng lẫy.

examples: He swelled with pride as he held the trophy. His family watched with pride from the bleachers.
He takes great pride in his work.
wiktionary.gloss: A sense of one's own worth; reasonable self-esteem and satisfaction (in oneself, in one's work, one's family, etc).

An unreasonable overestimation of one's own superiority in terms of talents, or looks, wealth, importance, etc., which comes across as being haughty, lofty, and often showing contempt of others; exaggerated self-worth.
Proud or disdainful behavior or treatment that reflects such an attitude (of haughtiness); arrogance.

examples: Her long ginger hair is her pride.
The 18th century table is the pride of Mark's house/
wiktionary.gloss: Something or someone of which one is proud; that which is the source of self-congratulation and self-esteem (whether reasonable or arrogant), for example
Show; ostentation; glory.
Highest level or rank; (figurative) elevation reached; loftiness or glory.
Consciousness of power; fullness of animal spirits; mettle; wantonness.
A group of lions or other large felines or similar animals.
The small European lamprey species Petromyzon branchialis.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English pryde, pride, from Old English prȳde, prȳte (“pride”) (compare Old Norse prýði (“bravery, pomp”)), derivative of Old English prūd (“proud”). More at proud. The verb derives from the noun, at least since the 12th century.

senses.definition: to feel proud of something you can do, have done, or own

examples.en: The hotel prides itself on offering excellent personal service.
examples.vi: Khách sạn tự hào về việc cung cấp dịch vụ cá nhân tuyệt vời.

senses.vi: lấy làm tự hào; tự hào về

thesaurus.definition: be proud of

vi_block: Lấy làm kiêu hãnh (về cái gì...).
Lấy làm tự hào (về việc gì...).

examples: I pride myself on being a good judge of character.
wiktionary.gloss: To take or experience pride in something; to be proud of it.

idioms.gloss: A person who is excessively proud will often suffer a setback or failure.
To set aside one's feelings of pride and adopt a more humble or appropriate stance.
To be proud of (usually followed by in or of).
With its tail feathers spread.
To swallow one's pride.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English raven, reven (“raven (Corvus corax); carrion crow (Corvus corone); rook (Corvus frugilegus) (?); the constellation Corvus; gall nuts of the Aleppo oak (Quercus infectoria) used to make black ink”), from Old English hræfn (“raven”), from Proto-West Germanic *hrabn (“raven”), from Proto-Germanic *hrabnaz (“raven”), probably from Proto-Indo-European *ḱrep- (“to crackle; to rattle”) or *ḱer- (“to croak, crow”), probably ultimately onomatopoeic, referring to the bird’s call.

senses.definition: a large bird with shiny black feathers and a harsh cry, related to the crow

examples.en: A black raven was sitting quietly on the branch.
examples.vi: Một con quạ đen đang đậu lặng lẽ trên cành cây.

examples.en: Ravens are known for their high intelligence and problem-solving skills.
examples.vi: Quạ đen nổi tiếng với trí thông minh cao và khả năng giải quyết vấn đề.

thesaurus.definition: large black bird with a straight bill and long wedge-shaped tail

wiktionary.gloss: Any of several, generally large, species of birds in the genus Corvus with lustrous black plumage; especially the common raven (Corvus corax).

examples: Near-synonyms: ebony, onyx
wiktionary.gloss: A jet-black, often glossy, colour, like that of the plumage of a raven (etymology 1, noun sense 1).
A flag bearing a raven (etymology 1, noun sense 1), formerly used by some Viking leaders
preceded by the: Viking military power.
A person, especially a man, with black hair.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English raven, reven (“raven (Corvus corax); carrion crow (Corvus corone); rook (Corvus frugilegus) (?); the constellation Corvus; gall nuts of the Aleppo oak (Quercus infectoria) used to make black ink”), from Old English hræfn (“raven”), from Proto-West Germanic *hrabn (“raven”), from Proto-Germanic *hrabnaz (“raven”), probably from Proto-Indo-European *ḱrep- (“to crackle; to rattle”) or *ḱer- (“to croak, crow”), probably ultimately onomatopoeic, referring to the bird’s call.

senses.definition: shiny and deep black in colour, usually used to describe someone's hair

examples.en: The princess was famous for her long raven hair and pale skin.
examples.vi: Nàng công chúa nổi tiếng với mái tóc đen nhánh dài và làn da trắng.

examples: Near-synonyms: ebony, onyx
raven curls    raven darkness
wiktionary.gloss: Of the jet-black and often glossy colour of the plumage of a raven (etymology 1, noun sense 1).

blocks.etymology: A variant of ravin, from Middle English ravin, ravine, raven (noun).

thesaurus.definition: obtain or seize by violence
prey on or hunt for
eat greedily

vi_block: Cắn xé (mồi); ăn ngấu nghiến, ăn phàm.

wiktionary.gloss: To absorb or take in (something, such as information) greedily; also, to approach or pounce on (someone) like prey.
Followed by about, after, or for: to go after or seek for something, especially booty or spoils; to maraud, to plunder; also (generally), to move about wildly and cause damage; to rampage.
To eat greedily; also, followed by on or upon: of an animal: to prey on.
Sometimes followed by about or on: to move about searching for food or prey ravenously.
Sometimes followed by after or for: to have a ravenous appetite or craving for food or prey.
Originally followed by with: to experience great hunger; to be ravenous.
To take and exploit or make use of greedily.
Sometimes followed by after or for: to have a strong craving or desire for, or to do, something; to crave, to desire, to yearn.

idioms.gloss: Synonym of as the crow flies.
